items.title: Here's an expert forecast for this weekend's gas prices in Ontario
items.summary: Dan McTeague, head of Canadians for Affordable Energy, offers his predictions for gas prices. Here’s a look at what’s happening with gasoline prices in Ontario. Ontario drivers feeling frustrated with the current high gas prices won’t get much relief this weekend. But on the bright side, prices aren’t expected to get much worse either. Here’s what you can expect from the pumps this weekend. Dan McTeague of Canadians for Affordable Energy, spoke with Metroland after energy markets closed Friday afternoon to offer his prediction for Ontario gasoline and diesel prices. What happens with energy markets is reflected at the pumps two days later. McTeague anticipates gasoline prices will drop by a penny per litre on Saturday and then rise by two cents on Sunday.

items.title: Battery fire prevention: What to know about lithium-ion batteries
items.summary: Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services shares practical tips to help residents reduce the risk of battery-related fires at home. Emergency and public safety | August 14, 2026 MFES has identified lithium-ion batteries as the city’s fastest-growing ignition source, recording a 122 per cent increase in lithium-ion battery-related fires in 2025 compared to the previous year. MFES responded to 20 incidents involving lithium-ion batteries in 2025 and has already responded to 15 incidents this year. Lithium-ion batteries power many of the devices we use every day, from cell phones and laptops to e-bikes and power tools. While these batteries are generally safe when used as intended, damaged, defective or improperly charged batteries can pose a serious fire risk. In some cases, damaged batteries can experience “thermal runaway,” a chain reaction that can cause intense heat, fire, toxic gases and, in some cases, explosions. This makes understanding how to safely use, charge and store these devices even more important, as it can help reduce the risk of fire. As the use of battery-powered devices continues to grow, MFES is encouraging residents to follow safe charging, storage and disposal practices to help prevent fires. Stop using the battery or device immediately if you notice signs of failure, such as swelling, unusual odours, excessive heat, discolouration, leaking fluids, smoke, vapour or strange noises. If a battery catches fire, move away from it and call 911. E.

items.title: Mississauga: Parrish and Crombie Tied; City Mood Turns Negative
items.summary: Carolyn Parrish and Bonnie Crombie are tied at 35% among decided and leaning voters, while more Mississauga residents say the city is moving in the wrong direction than the right direction. August 14, 2026 (Mississauga, ON) - A new Liaison Strategies Mississauga survey shows Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie tied among decided and leaning voters, while the city's overall mood has turned negative. If a mayoral election were held today, Parrish and Crombie would each receive 35% among decided and leaning voters, followed by Dipika Damerla at 18% and Alvin Tedjo at 12%. Among all voters, Parrish and Crombie are tied at 26% each, followed by Damerla at 13% and Tedjo at 9%. Twenty-six per cent are undecided. The survey also finds that 46% of Mississauga residents say the city is moving in the wrong direction, compared to 32% who say it is moving in the right direction and 22% who are not sure. Parrish's job approval is slightly underwater: 38% approve of the job she is doing as mayor, 42% disapprove, and 20% are not sure. Liaison surveyed a random sample of 1,000 Mississauga residents from August 11 to August 12, 2026, using Interactive Voice Recording (IVR) technology. Participants were reached through random digit dialling (RDD) across both landline and cellular phone networks. The resulting data was weighted to match targets based on the 2021 Census. 1 percentage points, 19 times out of 20. The margin is higher for sub-samples. Totals may not add up to 100% due to rounding. Liaison Strategies is one of the most accurate polling firms in Canada.

items.title: Ford's Backing of Parrish for Mississauga Mayor May Be Working Against Her, New Poll Suggests
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, a new Liaison Strategies poll suggests Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie are locked in a dead heat heading into the fall election, even though Ontario Premier Doug Ford has publicly backed Parrish's campaign. The poll, released Friday, found Parrish and Crombie would each take 26 per cent of the vote if the Oct. 26 election were held today, with another 26 per cent of voters still undecided. Councillors Dipika Damerla and Alvin Tedjo trailed with 13 per cent and nine per cent respectively, according to the poll. The Star reports Liaison principal David Valentin said none of the candidates has made a clear case for why voters should choose them over the others, leaving a large pool of undecided voters still up for grabs amid a broader sense the city is heading in the wrong direction. The Star notes an October 2025 Liaison poll also found Crombie and Parrish tied in a then-hypothetical matchup, before Crombie left to lead the Ontario Liberals and later resigned after the party's provincial election loss. Candidate registration for the fall municipal elections opened Friday as well.

items.title: City Warns E-Scooter Injuries Among Mississauga Kids Have Doubled in a Year
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, officials are reminding parents to keep children off e-scooters and e-bikes after a national report found 10 kids died from related injuries across Canada last year, six of them in Ontario. The city cites Canadian Paediatric Surveillance Program data showing 57 severe paediatric cases nationwide in 2025 involving death, an ICU admission or a hospital stay longer than two days, including 12 ICU admissions and 26 hospital stays beyond two days. The City of Mississauga notes e-scooters can be a convenient way for residents and visitors aged 16 and older to get around without a car, helping people connect to transit, school or work. But the city says local emergency department visits involving children aged 15 and under on e-scooters more than doubled between 2023 and 2024, rising from 34 visits to 72. Mississauga officials are using those numbers to urge parents to keep young children off the devices even as their popularity grows.

items.title: DavidsTea returns to Square One after closing 6 years ago in Mississauga
items.summary: Tea lovers rejoice — DavidsTea is back in Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga. The tea merchant officially announced the reopening in a press release today. “We are delighted to bring the full DavidsTea experience to consumers at Square One with our premium tea collections, wide assortment of accessories and expert recommendations from our Tea Guides,” said Sarah Segal, the company’s chief executive officer and chief brand officer. The shop, located on level two by entrance eight in Square One, celebrated their grand opening on Aug. 2. “A huge thank you to everyone who came by our opening event at Square One,” DavidsTea said on Instagram. ” Customers seemed thrilled with the shop’s return. “So happy to have you back close to home,” one person wrote on Instagram. “The store is beautiful and the staff is amazing! ” DavidsTea shut down 82 locations across Canada amid financial struggles in 2020, but last year the company announced a comeback. Stores were planned for Quebec City, Montreal and a location opened at the Oshawa Centre in June.

items.title: Halton Police Say a Mississauga Man Filmed a Woman in an Oakville Fitting Room
items.summary: According to INsauga, Halton Regional Police have charged a Mississauga man after a woman reported being filmed inside a change room at the Winners store on Winston Churchill Boulevard in Oakville on July 22. Police say the woman confronted the man after noticing him, but he fled the store before officers arrived. INsauga reports investigators later identified and arrested the suspect, 34-year-old Jeffrey Abou-Mechrek of Mississauga, charging him with one count of voyeurism. He was released with a future court date in Milton. Police released a photo of Abou-Mechrek because investigators are concerned there may be additional victims they haven't yet identified. Anyone who believes they may have been victimized, or who has information about the case, is asked to contact Halton's 2 District Criminal Investigations Bureau.
